claim: Jointly optimizing answer generation and confidence generation causes confidence-alignment RL objectives to interfere with and degrade answer accuracy, motivating a decoupled two-stage architecture where confidence is generated by a separate model conditioned on the fixed (question, answer) pair.
stance_target: design principle for verbal-confidence elicitation methods: decoupling improves reliability without sacrificing task accuracy
scope_conditions: MMLU, DROP, LogiQA2.0/ReClor; Llama-3-8B, Qwen3-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3
quoted_support: existing approaches jointly optimize answer generation and confidence generation. This coupling creates a crucial conflict: objectives designed to improve uncertainty estimation may alter the model's answer distribution and degrade task accuracy

claim: ORCE trains a confidence LLM with a Spearman-rank-correlation DPO reward against a sampling-based correctness-frequency surrogate (K completions per prompt), reducing ECE from 0.170 (vanilla) to 0.025 on Llama-3-8B/MMLU and from 0.212 to 0.034 on Qwen3-8B/MMLU, while exactly preserving answer accuracy.
stance_target: distilling a sampling-based surrogate into verbalized confidence via rank-based (not pointwise) RL substantially improves calibration
quoted_support: it obtains the lowest ECE on LLAMA-3 8B and Qwen3 8B, reducing ECE from 0.170 to 0.025 and from 0.212 to 0.034 compared with Vanilla, and substantially outperforming ConfTuner on both models.

claim: A global rank-correlation (Spearman) reward outperforms a local numeric-ranking-difference reward and a pointwise numeric-distance objective for aligning verbalized confidence with a sampling-based surrogate, per ablation on MMLU/Llama-3-8B.
stance_target: methodological choice: ranking-based losses are more effective than pointwise regression losses for calibrating verbalized confidence
quoted_support: Ours-ORCE achieves the best ECE, Spearman correlation, AURC, and E-AURC, demonstrating that global order-aware alignment is more effective than local rank-difference matching.

claim: ORCE's confidence LLM trained on Llama-3-8B transfers to Qwen3-8B and Mistral-7B with the best ECE and Spearman correlation among tested methods, without further training on the target model.
stance_target: cross-model generalizability of a decoupled, rank-based verbal confidence estimator
scope_conditions: MMLU, cross-model transfer from Llama-3-8B to Qwen3-8B and Mistral-7B
quoted_support: Ours-ORCE consistently achieves the best performance on both Qwen 7B and Mistral 7B, obtaining the lowest ECE, highest Spearman correlation, and lowest AURC/E-AURC across all transferred settings.

claim: ORCE is not tested on any code-generation benchmark; evaluation spans knowledge-intensive (MMLU), discrete (DROP), and logical (LogiQA2.0/ReClor) reasoning only.
stance_target: domain gap: rank-based confidence distillation has not been validated on code LLMs
quoted_support: We evaluate our method on three representative reasoning settings: MMLU for knowledge-intensive reasoning, DROP for discrete reasoning, and LogiQA 2.0 for logical reasoning.

claim: ORCE proves that optimizing Spearman rank correlation between verbalized confidence and a sampling-based surrogate recovers, at the population level, a monotone transform of the true prompt-level reliability function eta(x), i.e. rank-based alignment is theoretically sufficient for order-preserving calibration even without matching absolute probability values.
stance_target: theoretical justification for rank-based (AUROC-style) objectives over pointwise calibration (ECE-style) objectives when distilling a sampling signal into verbal confidence
scope_conditions: population-level analysis, Theorem 1, continuous-distribution assumptions on eta(X) and S(X,Y)
quoted_support: Theorem 1 shows that, at the population level, optimizing Spearman alignment recovers a score that is a monotone transform of the prompt-level reliability.

claim: ORCE cites ConfTuner's own Appendix F.6 as documenting that joint confidence-answer optimization degrades answer accuracy, establishing ConfTuner as the key prior RL-based verbal-confidence tuning method to benchmark against.
stance_target: identifies ConfTuner (Li et al. 2025, NeurIPS) as a load-bearing prior method for the literature review
quoted_support: objectives designed to improve uncertainty estimation may alter the model's answer distribution and degrade task accuracy (Appendix F.6 of [19])
